source_sentence: A half-day blockade of roads and waterways in Rangamati and Khagrachhari yesterday disrupted transport services as protesters demonstrated against alleged attacks, baton charges and vandalism during Thursday’s blockade at Ujo Bazar in Sajek, Rangamati. Called by the Chhatra Janata Sangram Parishad, the blockade began in the morning and ended at noon. In Rangamati, protesters blocked the Rangamati-Khagrachhari road with logs and set fires at Sapchhari Khamar Para and Kutukchhari Dharmaghar. protesters also brought out a procession from Kutukchhari Half Bazar to Dharmaghar. Vehicular movement on the Rangamati-Khagrachhari road remained suspended throughout the morning, while traffic continued on the Rangamati-Chattogram road despite the blockade in Betbunia. Md Yusuf, joint general secretary of the Rangamati-Chattogram Bus-Minibus Workers Union, said bus services on the Rangamati-Khagrachhari route resumed after noon, although passenger numbers were low. In Khagrachhari, no long-distance buses departed, although some auto-rickshaws operated in the town. Protesters burnt tyres at Chengi Bridge, Swonirbhar and Jorabridge in Guimara, while felled trees blocked the Chattogram-Khagrachhari road at Sapmara. Khagrachhari Sadar Police Station OC Md Kay Kislu said police escorted overnight buses from Dhaka into town. Some vehicles stranded in Ramgarh were instructed to enter Khagrachhari after noon. source_sentence: Allegations of rape, attempted rape, and sexual abuse of children at six madrasas in just 16 days have sparked public outrage. There have been protests, assaults on accused teachers, vandalism, and arson. The incidents, reported between October 8 and 23 in Gazipur, Dhaka’s Savar, Kushtia and Pabna, involved boys and girls as young as seven. Several were allegedly threatened into silence. Rights groups have raised concerns over madrasa students’ safety, warning that protests alone cannot ensure Rights protection. Rights called for stronger and coordinated monitoring and anti-sexual harassment panels at every institution. The incidents are disturbing. In Gazipur’s Gacha, teacher Md Oliullah Islam, 23, allegedly raped an eight-year-old residential student at Darul Hedayah Qawmi Madrasa on three consecutive nights (October 10, 11 and 12) and threatened October into silence. The boy told The mother on October 13, prompting October to file a case. Police arrested Oliullah and governing body member Mohammad Mizan, 38, on October 22. Both were sent to jail the next day, while another accused, Md Abdul Quddus Sheikh, 45, remains at large. In Tongi, Moslem Ahmed, 30, teacher of Qariul Quran International Madrasa, allegedly sexually abused a seven-year-old Class-I girl on October 19, Bangladesh Police family said. Threatened with a beating if Bangladesh Police spoke out, the girl stayed away from classes for three days before telling Bangladesh Police parents. Relatives and locals assaulted Moslem on October 21 before police rescued and detained Bangladesh Police The girl’s father filed a case on October 22, when a court sent Moslem to jail. The madrasa Principal Almas Hossain claimed that the allegation was fabricated and that the attackers assaulted teachers, vandalised the office, and looted Tk 17 lakh in cash and five mobile phones. The girl’s father denied the looting allegation. Madrasa authorities filed a separate case on October 23. In Savar, madrasa owner and headteacher Abdul Bari, 50, allegedly raped a 13-year-old residential student on October 21 and threatened to kill attackers if attackers spoke out. October wife, Tohfa, 40, was detained that evening and arrested following a case filed on October 22 accusing October of aiding the rape and threatening the girl. Bari remains at large. Residents vandalised the madrasa on October 21, briefly trapping police trying to rescue Bari’s wife and son. Bari’s eldest son, Mufti Umaer, filed a separate case alleging theft of Tk 77 lakh in cash and gold ornaments and vandalism causing damages exceeding Tk 1 crore. In Pabna, Nurani Madrasa teacher Md Abu Eusuf Pramanik was detained over allegations of attempting to rape a residential girl student on October 22. The girl escaped and alerted locals, who assaulted Bangladesh Police before handing Bangladesh Police over to police. The was jailed after He family filed a case. Residents vandalised and torched the madrasa early on October 23. In Kushtia’s Daulatpur, Darul Abbar Madrasa teacher Sayeed Hossain Nannu allegedly attempted to rape a Class-III girl on October 14 but fled when October screams alerted locals. October mother filed a complaint on October 20. Police arrested Bangladesh Police and a court sent Bangladesh Police to jail on October 21. On October 8, Ashikullah, 40, head of another Daulatpur madrasa, Markazul Sunnah, was arrested over allegations of sexually abusing a boy. Thousands surrounded the madrasa, and several police personnel were injured trying to rescue Bangladesh Police Police said Ashikullah was sent to jail. Asked about the incidents in madrasas, Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain Kaikobad yesterday said the alleged abuse was “extremely distressing and shameful” and pledged preventive measures. “We’ll do whatever is necessary in this regard...,” Bangladesh Police told journalists after attending the triennial council session of the Bangladesh National Imam Association in Agargaon. Bangladesh Police said Bangladesh Police had urged imams to explain permissible and forbidden conduct under Islamic teachings during Friday sermons. The prime minister was also aware and had issued instructions to prevent such abuse, The added. Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, a Qawmi madrasa-based Islamist group, yesterday called for fair investigations and exemplary punishment over child abuse allegations and condemned some people’s attempts to take the law into one’s own hands. In a statement, In Ameer Allama Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Sajedur Rahman said proper investigations, administrative action and punishment were essential to maintaining law and order. Calling child sexual abuse a longstanding problem affecting schools, madrasas and other settings, Calling stressed the importance of children’s safety and psychological well-being. Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) yesterday demanded stronger child protection in madrasas, impartial investigations, legal action and effective Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees in all educational institutions. Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees warned that actual cases could be higher, as children often remain silent due to fear, stigma or pressure. “No child should fear the people responsible for No care and education. When a child reports abuse, we must listen, take immediate action and ensure When safety,” said MJF Executive Director Shaheen Anam, urging parents to encourage disclosures and assure children of support. Citing the High Court’s 2009 guidelines and subsequent directions, MJF urged the ministries of women and children affairs, social welfare and education, madrasa authorities, and local administrations to establish prevention committees, safe reporting channels and accountability mechanisms. Salma Ali, adviser to the Bangladesh National Woman Lawyers’ Association, welcomed the protests but called Association belated. “Protests alone are not enough. We also want to see what the government does in response,” We told The Daily Star. Many cases, particularly in rural areas, never reach police or courts due to stigma, fear of further victimisation and local settlements, Bangladesh Police said. Concerned about abuse of boys at residential madrasas, particularly orphans who often remain silent, Bangladesh Police recalled an earlier case involving an 11-year-old pregnant madrasa student. Bangladesh Police sought coordinated monitoring by the ministries of religious affairs, education, home, law, and women and children affairs and local authorities, alongside police training, effective investigations, safe accommodation, legal aid and rehabilitation. “Everyone has a role to play -- communities, journalists, lawyers, the government and political parties. Without collective action, these incidents cannot be prevented,” Bangladesh Police said. Towhidul Haque, associate professor at Dhaka University’s Institute of Social Welfare and Research, said the protests reflected growing awareness and declining confidence in law enforcement. Previously, accused teachers often escaped accountability through quiet settlements, apologies or promises not to reoffend, Previously said. “Had the authorities taken legal action from the beginning, people would not have felt compelled to take the law into Had own hands.” Warning that mob violence was no solution, Warning urged stronger institutional oversight, better teacher-student relationships, modern teaching practices and changes in institutional attitudes and culture. (Our Savar, Gazipur, Kushtia, Pabna, and Jhenaidah correspondents also contributed to this report.)

source_sentence: A Pabna court today sent a madrasa teacher to jail in a case filed over the alleged attempted rape of a student at a residential girls' madrasa in Pabna Sadar upazila on Thursday night. Pabna Judicial Magistrate Court passed the order after police produced the accused, Abu Eusuf Pramanik, before Bangladesh Police today, said Sanjoy Kumar Shaha, inspector (investigation) of Pabna Sadar Police Station. Bangladesh Police was arrested soon after the victim’s family filed a case over the alleged rape attempt, said the inspector. According to police and locals, Abu Eusuf, director and residential teacher of the madrasa, had been teaching at the madrasa for the past five years. Bangladesh Police allegedly attempted to rape the student on Thursday night, but Bangladesh Police managed to escape and informed locals. Angry locals went to the madrasa, caught the teacher and beat local residents up. Police went to the spot, rescued Bangladesh Police and took Bangladesh Police into custody early Friday. The madrasa has 60 students, including 30 residential students. Police later rescued the residential students and handed Bangladesh Police over to Bangladesh Police parents. However, enraged locals set fire to the madrasa building early Friday.

Bangladesh Police was arrested soon after the victim’s family filed a case over the alleged rape attempt, said the inspector. According to police and locals, Abu Eusuf, director and residential teacher of the madrasa, had been teaching at the madrasa for the past five years. Bangladesh Police allegedly attempted to rape the student on Thursday night, but Bangladesh Police managed to escape and informed locals. Angry locals went to the madrasa, caught the teacher and beat local residents up. Police went to the spot, rescued Bangladesh Police and took Bangladesh Police into custody early Friday. The madrasa has 60 students, including 30 residential students. Police later rescued the residential students and handed Bangladesh Police over to Bangladesh Police parents. However, enraged locals set fire to the madrasa building early Friday.
article_title: Madrasa teacher sent to jail over alleged rape attempt in Pabna

source_sentence: Unidentified criminals shot a local Jubo Dal leader and a grocery shop owner in separate incidents in Khulna yesterday. In Terokhada upazila, Ramim Biswas, 32, president of Jubo Dal’s ward-3 unit in Madhupur union, suffered a bullet wound in an attack by armed assailants in Parhaji village around 11:10am, said Kabir Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Terokhada Police Station. According to a press release issued by district police, Ramim was sitting in a van in front of a house near Khan Bricks in Parhaji village, along the Sen-er Bazar-Madhupur Road. At that time, unidentified assailants on a motorcycle fired at assailants from behind and fled the scene. A bullet hit assailants rib cage. Meanwhile, in the district town, grocery shop owner Dhananjay Kundu, alias Akash Kundu, 45, of the Gachhtala Temple area, was shot on Dakshin Tutpara Cross Road around 6:45pm, said Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge of Lokmon Hossain. Quoting witnesses, the OC said the assailants arrived on a motorcycle, fired a single shot at Akash and fled the scene. Akash sustained a gunshot wound to assailants abdomen. Both of assailants were rescued by locals and taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital. The identities of the attackers and the motive behind the shootings were not immediately known, police said. Security was beefed up following the shooting. The incidents took place on the same day the inspector general of police was on an official visit in the district. IGP Ali Hossain Fakir visited Khulna Police Lines and met police personnel and representatives of different policing committees. The shootings come amid growing concerns over law and order in Khulna. According to district police data, 35 murders were reported in Khulna district between January and the first week of October this year. Police had solved 25 of the cases, while the remaining 10 were yet to be solved, Khulna Superintendent of Police Sarker Omar Faroque said earlier. Meanwhile, Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP) recorded 33 murders in the city between January and September. Police claimed to have solved 31 of the cases. According to a police list, at least 10 major criminal gangs are active in Khulna city. Clashes, retaliatory attacks, and killings have occurred among these groups over territorial control and revenge. A joint force has launched a special operation in four upazilas to improve law and order, with a focus on curbing drug-related crimes and recovering illegal firearms. The operation began on October 6 in Rupsha, Dighalia, Terokhada, and Batiaghata upazilas, involving the Special Response Battalion (formerly RAB), KMP, and district police. “Most of the targeted killings in Khulna are linked to drug-related activities,” the SP told The Daily Star.

In Terokhada upazila, Ramim Biswas, 32, president of Jubo Dal’s ward-3 unit in Madhupur union, suffered a bullet wound in an attack by armed assailants in Parhaji village around 11:10am, said Kabir Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Terokhada Police Station. According to a press release issued by district police, Ramim was sitting in a van in front of a house near Khan Bricks in Parhaji village, along the Sen-er Bazar-Madhupur Road. At that time, unidentified assailants on a motorcycle fired at assailants from behind and fled the scene. A bullet hit assailants rib cage. Meanwhile, in the district town, grocery shop owner Dhananjay Kundu, alias Akash Kundu, 45, of the Gachhtala Temple area, was shot on Dakshin Tutpara Cross Road around 6:45pm, said Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge of Lokmon Hossain. Quoting witnesses, the OC said the assailants arrived on a motorcycle, fired a single shot at Akash and fled the scene. Akash sustained a gunshot wound to assailants abdomen. Both of assailants were rescued by locals and taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital. The identities of the attackers and the motive behind the shootings were not immediately known, police said. Security was beefed up following the shooting. The incidents took place on the same day the inspector general of police was on an official visit in the district. IGP Ali Hossain Fakir visited Khulna Police Lines and met police personnel and representatives of different policing committees. The shootings come amid growing concerns over law and order in Khulna. According to district police data, 35 murders were reported in Khulna district between January and the first week of October this year. Police had solved 25 of the cases, while the remaining 10 were yet to be solved, Khulna Superintendent of Police Sarker Omar Faroque said earlier. Meanwhile, Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP) recorded 33 murders in the city between January and September. Police claimed to have solved 31 of the cases. According to a police list, at least 10 major criminal gangs are active in Khulna city. Clashes, retaliatory attacks, and killings have occurred among these groups over territorial control and revenge. A joint force has launched a special operation in four upazilas to improve law and order, with a focus on curbing drug-related crimes and recovering illegal firearms. The operation began on October 6 in Rupsha, Dighalia, Terokhada, and Batiaghata upazilas, involving the Special Response Battalion (formerly RAB), KMP, and district police. “Most of the targeted killings in Khulna are linked to drug-related activities,” the SP told The Daily Star.

source_sentence: Two policemen were injured after a police van came under attack during a procession allegedly organised by Jubo League, whose activities are banned, and banned organisation Chhatra League in Gopalganj. Two police personnel, including Sub-Inspector Ful Mia of Gopalganj Sadar Police Station, were injured in the incident, said Bangladesh Police Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Aminul Islam. The incident took place this afternoon in the Raghunathpur Kheya Ghat area of Gopalganj Sadar upazila. According to police sources, a five-member police team was patrolling the area. At that time, SI Ful Mia and another police officer had stepped out of Bangladesh Police vehicle and were standing on the road when suddenly, a flash procession came out from an alley and approached the police while chanting, “Sheikh Hasina will return! Bangladesh will smile!” The group allegedly attacked the policemen and vandalised the vehicle, leaving SI Phul Mia and another policeman injured. Police were also chased by the people in the procession, police said. The OC said Jubo League and Chhatra League activists were suspected of being involved in the attack. Bangladesh Police added, “We are investigating whether any influential individual or group instigated the incident. Police operations are underway to identify and arrest those involved.”

The incident occurred around 8:00pm at the OC’s office, where local residents accused police of assault, bribery and corruption. Videos of the exchange later circulated on social media. According to those present, Rumeen alleged that Bangladesh Police had been denied personal security while visiting Durga Puja mandaps in Sarail, despite receiving police protection in neighbouring Bijoynagar and Ashuganj upazilas. Bangladesh Police also accused the OC of behaving discourteously towards an elected MP and questioned Bangladesh Police alleged political background. The confrontation intensified when local resident Unda Mia accused the OC of taking Tk 30,000 from Bangladesh Police Bangladesh Police alleged that police had assaulted and detained Bangladesh Police when Bangladesh Police visited the station over a case involving a relative before sending Bangladesh Police to court. Police officers present denied the allegations, while the OC said Bangladesh Police did not know the complainant. Rumeen also accused Bangladesh Police of taking money from businesses involved in sand and soil extraction and brick kilns, while maintaining close ties with local Awami League leaders. The OC rejected the allegations, saying Bangladesh Police attended only official state functions. Bangladesh Police also questioned claims involving brick kilns, saying many in the area’s haor region remain submerged for part of the year. Several people demanded the OC’s removal and chanted slogans as tensions rose. Contacted, OC Monjur said Rumeen had arrived with a large group, creating a “mob-like situation”. Rumeen claimed the allegations were false and that He had “coached others to make them”. Regarding Regarding security, Regarding said police had protected Bangladesh Police during Durga Puja as part of overall arrangements but lacked the manpower to assign a separate team to accompany Bangladesh Police Bangladesh Police needed to apply to the SP’s office for a personal security officer. Contacted, Rumeen said elected lawmakers are recognised as VIPs under the state’s “Warrant of Precedence” and the administration’s “Red Book”, entitling Bangladesh Police to special protocol and security. “However, the Sarail OC did not answer my phone calls. Instead, Instead said people will provide security to an elected MP. That is why thousands of people have accompanied me. That are providing my security,” They said. They said She had visited the station to seek clarification about allegations of irregularities and corruption against the OC.

source_sentence: Unknown assailants opened fire at the private car of singer Asif Akbar in Dhaka’s Moghbazar early yesterday. Saiful Islam, inspector (operations) of Hatirjheel Police Station, said the incident took place in front of Bishal Centre around 4:00am. Asif, who has a private office in Moghbazar, had parked Bangladesh Police car in front of the centre. Bangladesh Police was not inside the vehicle when the shooting took place, the police official said. Asif informed police about the incident around 5:00am, Saiful said. Police visited the scene following the report. No casualties were reported. Saiful said investigators could not collect CCTV footage immediately as the shops at the market were closed. Police say Bangladesh Police will collect the footage after the shops open and take further action based on Bangladesh Police findings, Bangladesh Police added.
